opening.argument: The speaker urges viewers to buy Luna before a snapshot to qualify for a new-token airdrop, stating that holders “will be entitled to receive an airdrop of the new LUNA” and that people would buy before the snapshot and sell afterward. He presents possible returns ranging from 10% to doubling, tripling, or quadrupling, making the timing-sensitive purchase attractive despite uncertainty about the proposal. He also directs viewers to Voyager, offers a $25 Bitcoin benefit, and characterizes the resulting Luna exposure as “zero-risk” because the reward would offset a loss. Although he acknowledges that the price could fall afterward and says he does not know the exact proposal, those qualifications do not remove the buy-in pitch or its unsupported risk-free characterization.
